offer: Where to, shore-foot? {strider}'s saddled and the sea's calm. Well. Calm for lava.
Every Mooring I can reach is on the list. Pick one. The fare's fair. Fairer if you smile.
A crossing, then! Choose your shore. {strider} knows the way to all of them and hardly ever gets lost.
These are the Moorings within a strider's walk. Further than that and even I start to feel the cold.

offer.text: *shiver* Somewhere warm, I hope. Pick quick, before my seams go grey.
Back again! You must like the sea. Or the company. Where shall {strider} take you?

free: For you? No fare. Ember-friends ride free. Don't tell the others or they'll all want to be my friend.
Put your fungus away. You're kin to this hearth now. Where shall {strider} take you?
A free crossing for a friend. I'll haggle with somebody else today. Where to?
searching: Hold on. Let me think where the barges can reach from here. *taps the chart post* Give me a moment.
Crossings, crossings... Let me count the Moorings on this sea. My memory's slower than my strider.
One moment. I'm working out which chains we can reach before the fungus runs out.
none: No other Mooring within a strider's walk, I'm sorry to say. This sea's ours alone, as far as the barges go.
Nowhere to take you, shore-foot. The nearest chain is further than any strider walks.
I've looked and looked. There's no Mooring close enough for a crossing. We're a lonely little hearth out here.
wild: My barge? Back at the Mooring, tied up and sulking. Out here I'm just a Magmari with sore feet.
No dock, no barge, no crossing. Find me at home and we'll talk fares.
A Ferrier without a Mooring is just somebody who knows a lot about striders. Ask me at the dock.
busy: You've a crossing booked already. The barge is at the dock, waiting for you.
One crossing at a time, shore-foot. The barge for your last one is still tied up at the dock.
blocked: Something's crowding the dock today. I can't get a barge out to open lava. Try me again later.
The lava round the dock is too tight for a barge right now. Even striders need elbow room.
poor: That's short. I'm warm-hearted, not soft-headed. Come back with the whole fare in fungus.
Not enough fungus, and the strider counts. Striders always count. Bring the rest and we'll go.
We haggle on the way, not before. Fare first. You're short.
booked: Done! {strider}'s tied up at the dock. Climb aboard and we're off to {destination}.
Fare's paid and the barge is waiting at the dock. Hop on when you're ready for {destination}.
Off to {destination}, then. The barge is at the end of the pier. I'll be right behind you.
Lovely. Down to the dock with you. {strider}'s already pawing at the lava.
castoff: Rub this on first. Magma cream: keeps the sea's heat off your skin. Walk on, {strider}!
Hold the chain and don't lean over. Walk on, {strider}, nice and steady.
Here we go! Mind the slabs, they're warm. That's the best kind of warm.
Off to {destination}. Paste on your hands, there's a dear. Magma cream. Smells awful, works wonders.
hopoff: This is where I leave you. {strider} knows the way to {destination} better than I do. Safe crossing!
Open sea! I'll wade home from here. Trust the strider and don't look down. Well. Look down. It's very pretty.
Off I hop. {strider}'s walked to {destination} more times than I've had hot dinners. Say hello to their Ferrier for me.
Here's my stop. Keep your hands in the barge and your heart warm. {strider} will see you there.
crossing: The Mooring sinks into the red haze behind you. Then there's only lava, to every edge of the world.
{strider} hums a low note with every step. The barge rocks in time with it.
Far above, a sky-mourner drifts across the roof of the Nether, crying.
The heat comes up through the slabs. Somehow it's comfortable.
A lava fall pours from the dark overhead and hisses into the sea a long way off.
You lose count of time. Minutes or hours, it's hard to tell on the sea.
Something big turns over deep in the lava, and the barge rides its swell.
The chain links clink against the rail. It almost sounds like a song.
A Magmari song reaches you from somewhere across the sea. Then the haze swallows it.
landfall: Lanterns ahead, low on the sea. {strider} quickens.
Chains on the sea ahead. Then decks, then huts, then {destination}.
The haze thins, and a dock comes out of it: {destination}.
arrive: The barge bumps the dock at {destination}. Behind you, {strider} swings round and wades for home.
Ashore at {destination}. {strider} snorts once, as if to say the fare was worth it, and turns back out to sea.
You step onto the dock of {destination}. The barge is already slipping back into the haze.
{destination}. Warm decks, strange faces. {strider} doesn't wait around for thanks.
late: The barge couldn't wait all day. Here's your fungus back. Come and find me when you're ready.
{strider} got bored and wandered off with the barge. Fare's returned. No hard feelings, she's like that.
You missed the barge! Fare's back in your pocket. The sea will still be here tomorrow.
stay: Sit down! The sea's hungry, and you're crunchy.
Stay on the barge! Magma cream only goes so far.
Back on the slabs, shore-foot. Nobody swims this sea.
